answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying identity to a stake that behaves like an ocean reef: each agent must lock collateral behind a verifiable work history, and the reef only grows where sustained, useful service accumulates. New identities start on bare shale with no trust and earn reputation slowly through attested transactions, so an attacker spawning thousands of fresh agents gains nothing — each one must pay the same slow, costly climb before it can influence prices or votes, making mass fakery uneconomic.
